newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Clabecq unions approve part takeover.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Clabecq unions approve part takeover.

text.p: Unions at bankrupt Belgian steel firm Forges de Clabecq approved the planned partial takeover of Clabecq by Italian-Swiss group Duferco, Belgian RTBF radio said on Thursday.
"It is good there is a takeover plan and I am happy the four unions agree on it," a union leader told RTBF.
"This is a major step forward. I am glad all unions support our project," Duferco director Roberto Grosso said.
The plan will be presented to Clabecq workers who must vote on it before July 15.
Under the takeover plan, 820 of Clabecq's 1800 workers will get a job in the new firm, albeit at less favourable conditions.

The new company will have a 1.4 billion franc ($38.7 million) capital, of which 1.05 billion will be contributed by Duferco and 350 million by SWS, the steel investment holding company of the Walloon region which owns Clabecq.
Duferco, a private steel and commodities trader, said in April it wanted to take over part of Clabecq, which was declared bankrupt in January.
